newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Gambro sees increased margins in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Gambro sees increased margins in 1997.

text.p: Swedish medical technology company Gambro, held by investment company Incentive AB, said on Monday it expected margins to increase in the rest of 1997.
"I expect that volumes, sales and the operating margin will improve in the coming three quarters," Gambro chief executive Berthold Lindqvist told an analyst meeting.

Gambro's first quarter operating margin fell to 11.9 percent from 12.5 percent in the corresponding 1996 quarter, but operating profit rose to 345 million crowns from 327 million and sales advanced to 2.90 billion from 2.62 billion.
"We have had 15 million crowns in costs for currency hedging and this has hampered operating profit," Lindqvist said, explaining the fall.
Such costs did not occur in the year earlier quarter and for the full-year 1997 there will be a negative effect of about 30 million crowns at current foreign exchange rates, he said.
The margin was hurt as dialysis care with lower margins make up a larger part of sales after a string of U.S. acquisitions, he said.
"We have initially focused on university facilities which give a low initial cost but at the same time a lower operating margin," he said.
In addition, production disruptions within dialysis products, a field with relatively high margins, had a negative impact on the operating margin.
